tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: A Property Tax Bill of Rs 195.06 crs. was received, which comprised of Rs. 11.46 Cr. and rest towards past period. The Company has challenged the said demand by filing an IA in the pending Writ Petition. On the basis of earlier stay order the Court directed deposit of Rs. 5 crs within 4 weeks and stayed the entire impugned Demand. In compliance of the said Order, Rs. 5 crs was deposited. Further, property tax bill demanding Rs.11.45 Crs showing tax arrears of Rs.190 Crores was issued by NDMC to IHCL. IHCL has issued a reply to NDMC apprising that in view of stay granted by the Delhi High Court on earlier occasions in the pending writ petition, there is no basis to seek recovery of amount mentioned in the bill. Application seeking stay of such demand filed and pending for hearing.

tax_litigation.status: Delhi High Court stayed the demand under Property Tax bill dated 28.05.2025 subject to deposit of Rs. 2 Crores by IHCL with NDMC within 4 weeks. In compliance of the same Rs. 2 Crores stands deposited with NDMC by IHCL.

operating_notes.text: Enterprise revenue crossed ₹17,000 Cr across brands.
Domestic RevPAR grew 14% in Q1FY27, with Rajasthan and Goa up 27-29% and Mumbai, Delhi and Bangalore up 12-13%.
Portfolio stood at 645 hotels (382 operational, about 265 in the pipeline) and is expected to cross 650 in July 2026.
Ginger revenue was ₹183 Cr (+20% YoY, 39% EBITDA margin); Brij's 11 hotels did ₹11 Cr (+42%) and Atmantan ₹19 Cr (+19%).
IHCL portfolio reached 400 operational hotels in Q2FY27 with 670 total hotels including pipeline.

Melisa Alva, Senior Vice President & Company Secretary, shared the Q4-FY26 earnings call recording on May 11, 2026, via the company’s IR website.
The Indian Hotels Company reported Q4FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹2,845 Cr, up 14% YoY, and FY26 PAT exceeding ₹2,000 Cr.
